A. Does recent evidence support the size of effect we assume: does this measure reduce deaths among the people it reaches, and by how much?
Measure: Smoking cessation started at the first specialist visit. Every current smoker with suspected lung cancer gets cessation medication and counselling at the first visit, as part of preparing for curative treatment.
effect_summary_en: A prospective cohort of 517 current smokers with early-stage NSCLC found that those who quit after diagnosis had lower all-cause mortality (adjusted HR 0.67, 95% CI 0.53–0.85).
supported_en: In 517 early-stage NSCLC smokers in Moscow, quitting after diagnosis was linked to lower all-cause mortality (HR 0.67), according to the Annals of Internal Medicine (2021).
not_supported_en: The study is observational and Russian. It does not show how many patients a first-visit programme would actually get to quit.
summary_en: We found no public sign that HUS or Keusote starts quit-smoking medicine and counselling at the first specialist visit for suspected lung cancer. HUS's pathway page says a nurse gives guidance at the first visit and that quitting completely is key, and Keusote offers a digital quit programme and prescriptions through the patient's own care team. A 2021 cohort study in the Annals of Internal Medicine found that quitting after diagnosis was linked to lower all-cause mortality in early-stage NSCLC (HR 0.67, 95% CI 0.53–0.85), which matches what our model assumes.
unanswered_en: Three searches found no HUS or Keusote page describing a standing order for quit-smoking medicine at the first lung cancer visit, and none describing a smoke-free surgery service run by a quit-smoking nurse.
